chapter_summary: An old mark outlasts any known account of its maker. Debolina feels kinship with that hand while resisting the romance of its disappearance.

history.status: grounded in the declared setting only
flagged_uncertainties: The anonymity of Shekhawati mural painters is a theme of the source, not a documented finding; the poem must not claim every maker was anonymous.

spatality.place: an old panel in the oldest part of a haveli, above head height
spatality.route: up the scaffold to the oldest layer, then down again
spatality.texture: faded ochre, a surface worn smooth where hands have touched it

poetic_parameters.movement: Language Poetry — the fragment as the only complete statement, here a hand with no name.
writing_skills: address to an absent maker rather than a present object
refusal of the consolation of anonymity
an ending that keeps the difference between kinship and equality
poetic_parameters.image_seed: an old ochre stroke worn smooth, its maker's gesture still legible
poetic_parameters.volta: from claiming kinship with the anonymous hand to refusing to make its erasure beautiful
poetic_parameters.sonic_texture: soft h and w in hand, who, wore, and the dry fricative of faded
poetic_parameters.line_gesture: elegiac medium lines that lengthen at the volta, then break
poetic_parameters.variety_note: Chapter twenty travelled to another town; this poem travels backward in time to a single unknown hand and refuses the romance of its loss.
poetic_parameters.metaphor_family: worn stroke, unrecorded name, and kinship that does not flatter
poetic_parameters.address: the anonymous painter, in the second person
poetic_parameters.closing_move: a refusal — the poem declines to call the silence holy
